speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: asked Minister for Social and Family Development (a) since the publication of the national guide for early childhood educators on Outdoor Learning by the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) in September 2019, whether the Ministry has taken stock of how many preschools are implementing the recommendations in the guide; (b) if so, what is the progress; (c) what are the challenges encountered by preschool operators incorporating more outdoor time in their curriculum; and (d) how is the Ministry helping to address these challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Outdoor learning is a critical part of the holistic learning and the development of young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We have increased the emphasis of outdoor learning in our refreshed curriculum frameworks introduced in 2022 and 2023 so that preschools will plan for children’s outdoor learning experiences across various domains, for example, numeracy, language and literacy, instead of only focusing on physical development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In addition, all preschools are required to incorporate gross motor activities into their curriculum, of which a specified amount must be done outdoors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The national guide on outdoor learning was developed to provide educators with guiding principles and practical suggestions to enhance children’s learning in the outdoors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Instead, the recommendations were weaved into ECDA’s Outdoor Learning Training Programme for preschools while ideas on outdoor learning were shared on an online repository.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: With the support of the Temasek Foundation, trained educators also held peer sharing sessions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Many of them have indicated the training courses contributed to their increased confidence in planning and implementing outdoor learning experiences for children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Challenges faced by preschools in implementing outdoor learning activities include child safety and management in outdoor spaces as well as dedicating time for outdoor activities in the timetable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Through the training courses and peer sharing sessions, educators learnt how to overcome these challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, educators learnt practical strategies to enhance child safety and management outdoors and gained ideas to creatively use existing time and space for outdoor learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Another challenge faced is that some preschools may not have safe and accessible spaces for outdoor learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Beyond preschools' enhanced learning outdoors, families have the most important role in ensuring their children spend time outdoors playing and learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: With concerted efforts from all stakeholders, we believe that outdoor learning will become an integral part of our children’s everyday life and development.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I thank the Minister of State for her answer.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I am quite heartened to know that the Ministry is taking a rather capacity building-based approach and involving the Temasek Foundation to advance this course to ensure more outdoor learning for children.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I can imagine that, given the challenges, some of that might come from resistance from parents, especially on the one about safety.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I can also imagine that this puts additional pressure on the preschool educators who might feel uncomfortable or that they are at risk if parents come and give feedback or complain about the children getting hurt while playing outdoors.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So, does the Ministry plan to form any kind of educational outreach or dialogues with parents to also educate parents on the benefits of outdoor curriculum so that they can be an equal partner and stakeholder in this effort?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And I would like to be more specific about this request because outdoor spaces can mean highly manicured and curated gardens with bonsai and flowers and all that versus a naturalistic, very natural environment where children can learn the principles of nature and the ecosystem at work.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, parents are very important stakeholders in this process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our various preschools frequently update parents about the kind of activities that are happening in preschools.
